module.summary: 从自由能梯度项到空间畴壁，再在独立SSH模型中观察界面电子态。

lessons.title: From equivalent domains to domain wall in space
lessons.summary: With the same two minimum values, why can the interface be neither infinitely steep nor infinitely wide?

sections.title: Add gradient cost to local free energy
sections.text: There have been phase transition experiments to find uniform minima. After letting φ change with the position, the local double well hopes to take ±v everywhere, and the gradient term hopes that the adjacent positions will be smooth; the two compete to determine the wall width.

sections.title: Fix the boundary and find the stationary point
sections.text: Fix the left endpoint at −v and the right at +v, then vary the interior φ. Boundary variations vanish; integration by parts gives a second-order equation. Choose the interface center at x=0.

sections.title: Continuous solution and width
sections.text: On the infinite domain, a tanh profile connects the two minima. Larger κ penalizes abrupt spatial changes and widens the wall; larger v or β strengthens the local restoring force.

sections.title: Teaching amount and material amount
sections.text: Here x, φ, and free energy are all in reduced units. BaTiO₃ only provides the background of 180° polar domain ; to calculate the material wall energy, real coefficients, electrostatic boundaries and elastic coupling are required.

lessons.title: Domain-wall energy and grid convergence
lessons.summary: Compare analytic tension, finite intervals, and discrete solutions, and understand the use of computational diagnostics.

sections.title: Wall energy is an additional price for a relatively homogeneous bulk phase
sections.text: Set the uniform ground state free energy at both ends to zero. The gradient term on the continuous equilibrium solution is equal to the local potential energy; integrating over the entire space yields the wall energy per area.

sections.title: Make a comparison that can be calculated by hand
sections.text: Fixed β=v=1 and changed κ from 1 to 4. Both width and wall energy are doubled. Wider walls do not necessarily mean cheaper, because what changes is the model parameters.

sections.title: The role of two grids
sections.text: program fixes the same finite interval and uses N and 2N-1 points to find discrete stationary points. The energy difference is an indication of the current discreteness sensitivity; a small stationary point residual does not mean that the continuous solution has converged.

sections.title: Stability and model boundaries
sections.text: The two boundary conditions force one wall to exist, while antisymmetry pins its center. This experiment finds a center-constrained static stationary point and also checks the Hessian after releasing that constraint. Coarse grids can create unstable directions, so a small residual alone does not establish stability. Domain nucleation, switching speeds and 3D domain morphology are not predicted.

lessons.title: SSH domain wall How to generate localized electronic states
lessons.summary: puts the inversion of bond order, finite chain energy spectrum and local density of states into the same research picture.

sections.title: Use bond order as another order parameter
sections.text: In the independent SSH model, alternating strong and weak bonds define dimerization order. Reverse it smoothly at the center and compare with uniform dimerization. Interface width uses bond spacings and is not equated numerically to a ferroelectric wall width.

sections.title: Pairing of Chiral Symmetry and Spectrum
sections.text: Without onsite potentials, the even/odd sublattice-sign operator anticommutes with the Hamiltonian, pairing energies ±E. Onsite potentials on the central two sites break this symmetry and change local spectra.

sections.title: Why look at energy and position at the same time?
sections.text: open chain can have terminal states and interface states at the same time, and the limited length will also cause hybridization. Observing the LDOS near E=0 and the center/boundary weights can distinguish the two. When the link is short or the interface is wide, the two areas may overlap. You need to check the area index and warning. Do not add the two weights.

sections.title: avoids the influence of arbitrary degenerate eigenvectors
sections.text: program treats all states of |E|<tδ as a subspace, and uses projection operator diagonal elements to display its density; the sum of densities is equal to the number of selected states. This quantity is unchanged within the selected subspace change of basis .

exercises.title: Get the width of domain wall step by step

steps.hint: Observe whether it contains position derivatives.
steps.explanation: Gradient terms impose energy costs on rapid spatial changes.

steps.prompt: What is the stationary point equation given by fixed boundary variation?
steps.hint: The gradient term needs to be integrated by parts.

steps.prompt: Substituting φ=v tanh(x/ξ), what is ξ?
steps.hint: Compare the coefficients multiplying tanh and sech².

steps.prompt: Only increases κ by 4 times, how does ξ change?
steps.explanation: The gradient cost becomes larger and the equilibrium wall width increases by 2 times.

exercises.title: Wall energy and numerical reliability
exercises.prompt: Check the baseline model and κ=4 model.

steps.prompt: What is the benchmark infinite continuous wall energy?
κ=4 What is the wall energy when β and v are constant?
steps.hint: Wall energy is also proportional to √κ.
steps.explanation: Both wall width and wall energy are increased by 2 times.

steps.prompt: The stationary point residual error is very small, but the grid energy difference is obvious. What should be done?
steps.hint: Discrete equations and continuous limits are two different tests.
choices: is directly called the precise material wall energy
Add grid and compare the same intervals
steps.explanation: The discrete error needs to be checked and the limited interval extended if necessary.

steps.prompt: Can the current energy be quoted directly as a BaTiO₃ wall energy in J/m²?
steps.hint: No true length/polarization/energy scales are given here.
choices: As long as the curve is smooth
No, material coefficient and unit scale are required
steps.explanation: The reduced teaching model only describes the mechanism and parameter scaling.

exercises.title: Distinguish between interface state and terminal state
exercises.prompt: Compare the wall-ssh, uniform-chain and central-onsite-potential presets.

steps.prompt: Which quantity changes sign across space in the SSH experiment?
steps.hint: Observe adjacent strong and weak bonds.
steps.explanation: A sign reversal of alternating hopping connects two bond-order patterns.

steps.prompt: Which relationship holds when there is no potential?
steps.hint: Γ has opposite signs on the two sublattices.
steps.explanation: Chiral symmetry leads to ±E energy spectrum pairing, and finite chains can still have hybrid splitting.

steps.prompt: After discovering the near-zero energy level, how to confirm that it is at the interface?
choices: Only look at the absolute value of energy
Look at the LDOS/projection weights of the center and borders simultaneously
steps.explanation: Open chains may also have terminal states, requiring position-resolved evidence.

steps.prompt: When two nearly degenerate states are replaced by a set of orthogonal basis, which quantity remains unchanged?
choices: Each component of an arbitrary eigenvector
steps.explanation: is unchanged for the unitary change of basis inside the selected subspace.

cases.title: BaTiO₃ Background: From polar domain to scalar wall
cases.summary: Starting from the existing polar distortion and six directional domains, select two opposite domains to construct a one-dimensional continuous wall.
cases.assumption: Scalar 180° teaching wall; does not include material fitting, elastic and electrostatic boundaries.
links: Uniform phase transition and directional domain

cases.title: Dimerization chain: interface and terminal states appear simultaneously
cases.summary: Use finite-chain energy spectra, LDOS, and projector densities to distinguish interface and boundary contributions.
cases.assumption: is a spin-free, non-interaction one-dimensional model, not a polyacetylene material parameter fitting.

cases.title: How does local potential change the interface spectrum?
cases.summary: Keep hopping and chain length fixed. Add a potential only at the central two sites and compare the chiral-symmetry residual and LDOS.
cases.assumption: Local onsite potentials break chiral symmetry; moving energy levels can change threshold selection of the near-zero-energy subspace.
